page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m2.large is a burstable, entry-level virtual server instance belonging to the shared-core t6 family. Powered by a KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 2 vCPUs backed by a single physical core and two threads on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU features 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for vector extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside AES cryptographic instructions.

System memory totals 4.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Benchmark results indicate conservative throughput profiles consistent with budget-oriented shared infrastructure. The memory subsystem delivers 20.68 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 16.39 GB/sec in large-block write operations, placing it in the lower quartile of observed memory bandwidth tests. Synthetic CPU metrics reflect its shared and burstable scheduling, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 2,464.26, a Geekbench single-core score of 1,045.0, and a multi-core score of 1,850.0.

The hardware configuration includes no integrated local storage and no dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs. Networking defaults to a baseline bandwidth of 0 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are attached. Application benchmarks demonstrate basic service capabilities, achieving 2.57 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.44 GB/sec throughput in static web serving tasks. For lightweight inference utilizing a 135M parameter language model, it handles 97.08 tokens per second during prompt ingestion and 21.85 tokens per second during generation.

Because of its shared-core model and burstable CPU credit allocation, ecs.t6-c1m2.large provides a low-cost compute entry point with clear operational tradeoffs. Sustained high-utilization workloads will quickly encounter processing limits. The instance is best suited for non-production environments, code repositories, microservices with intermittent activity, low-traffic web hosting, and development or testing sandboxes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m2.large is a burstable shared-core virtual instance designed for lightweight and intermittent computing demands. Built on x86_64 architecture and managed by KVM, it provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor at 2.5 GHz, paired with 4.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks bundled local storage, network baseline throughput, and GPU acceleration. Benchmark assessments place its performance across CPU, memory bandwidth, and operational tests within the entry-tier bracket, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 1,850.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 2,464.26. The burstable CPU allocation offers a cost-effective footprint for non-continuous workloads, though it is constrained by limited sustained throughput and memory capacity. It is primarily suitable for development environments, test beds, small static web servers, and intermittent microservices.
